significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: after a fact is read, a "graded and selective" internal-ripple magnitude across entailment types predicts whether each later ripple query will be answered correctly, thereby fixing expectations about which logical consequences are precomputed rather than derived on demand. This establishes a substantial phenomenon and a representational correlate, though not yet a full causal mechanism; it would distinguish ingestion-time propagation failure from query-time retrieval or reasoning failure, an explanatory ambiguity underlying behavioral consistency tests such as Cohen et al.'s RippleEdits and inverse-relation failures exemplified by the Reversal Curse. Verified false, especially if the signal is absent under the stated logical-selectivity conditions, would rule against spontaneous read-time propagation and support on-demand computation, so the branches are determinate and both informative. In the topic-substitution check, replacing the predictive read-time ripple with generic "research on LLM beliefs" would not preserve this score: the measurable pre-query coupling and precompute-versus-on-demand distinction are specific additions beyond the topic-median probe hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "read-time internal-ripple diagnostic," whose magnitude is proposed to forecast downstream ripple-QA success; it is ex ante because it fires after ingestion but "before any query," leaving an action window for context-management, editing, or reliability gating. What transfers is not merely a probe-finding procedure but the asserted predictive relation between ripple magnitude and later correctness across "symmetric relations, inverse relations, transitive/multi-hop, [and] type-inheritance," although each new model would still require probe re-extraction and calibration. The hypothesis is phrased across LLMs and classes of entailments, with downstream uptake extending to people operating "editing pipelines, context-management, and reliability evaluations," but it does not assert a quantitative invariant across architectures or meaningful uptake outside AI. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic internal belief representations provide neither this pre-outcome predictor nor the associated screening and gating handle.
